label: Evidence 3 model: LightGBM, one snapshot (Jan 2026)
reason: Starting point, so we can tell what each later change adds.

label: LightGBM, four snapshots (Oct 2025 to Jan 2026)
change: Train on four monthly snapshots instead of one.
reason: One snapshot depends on a single season. More rows and more months should make the ranking steadier.

label: LightGBM, four snapshots plus three new features
change: Add spend trend, active months in the last three and non-OXXO share of the last three months.
reason: The model saw purchase counts moving. Spend and recent non-OXXO behavior are closer to what a flip-out is.

label: LightGBM, six snapshots (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026)
change: Add the February and March 2026 snapshots to the training data.
reason: v2 stopped in January, four months before the test. Months closer to the test should look more like it.

label: LightGBM, six snapshots, recent months weighted more
change: Same data as v4, but each newer month counts more in training (weight 1 for October up to 2 for March).
reason: If users change habits over the year, the model should learn more from the latest months than from the oldest.

label: v5 plus payday behavior
change: Add how much more each user buys on payday than the calendar predicts, over 6 months and the last 3, and its trend.
reason: Our team question was whether payday changes spending. If it does, it should help tell who flips out.

label: v6 plus a 12-month view of the OXXO share
change: Add the OXXO share over the last 12 months: average, spread, highest, lowest, and the gap between the last month and the average.
reason: Six months can hide a user who was far from OXXO earlier in the year. A full year shows how stable the habit really is.
